annotations.text:
Chosen 2026-09-16: Sheet's design language on Directory's layout.
From Sheet: Cabin with Fira Code, sheet paper with Landranger magenta, the extent locators in the tree and beside the layer title, the map drawn as a survey sheet with margin coordinates.
From Directory: the parsed URL as the window's spine, the document-style layer page that answers 'can I get this out?' in one sentence, the transfers strip along the bottom, the map as a tab.
The three original directions are on the Directions page.

Three directions for ArcGIS Explorer, each pairing a token set with a spine. They mix: Stratum tokens with the Directory path bar is a valid fourth. Each frame has a dark toggle above it. Content is a fictional council server (Ashcombe) with a real-shaped LLPG layer, so the verdicts, counts and fields are the kind you will see, not lorem ipsum.

A · Stratum (family). DuckLake Explorer's tokens as they are: Hanken Grotesk with JetBrains Mono, limestone by day and JetBrains Islands by night, ink teal and brass. The left rail becomes the transfer log where DuckLake has the snapshot log, and the chunk grid is the signature in place of the core sample.
Why: one Theme, fonts already bundled, family resemblance for free.
Tradeoff: nothing in the chrome says ArcGIS. The URL you paste first is nowhere to be seen.

B · Directory. Its own identity, taken from the thing every GIS engineer already knows: the ArcGIS REST services directory. The parsed URL is the spine of the window, every node is a link, and the layer page reads like a document that answers 'can I get this out?' in one sentence. IBM Plex Sans and Mono, paper white with ultramarine links, blue slate at night.
Why: the product is URL-first, so the interface is.
Tradeoff: a second token set to build beside Stratum, and the map is a tab rather than always on.

C · Sheet. Its own identity, taken from the survey sheet: extents and spatial references are the app's real subject, so every node carries a locator and the map is always on, drawn with sheet margins and grid coordinates. Cabin (Gill lineage, like OS map covers) with Fira Code; pale sheet paper with Landranger magenta.
Why: you see where a layer is and how big it is before you touch it.
Tradeoff: the widest layout, and a third of the window goes to the map even when you only want the fields.
